title: tap: Adding flags for tap_packet_cb
description: This allows flags to be passed by the registering listener to the collection of information. The main intent is, to steer, how collective information is being generated for conversations and endpoints (future change), but it can be used for a variety of other usecases as well.

notes.body:
added 1 commit
  • 7fdd684e - tap: Adding flags for tap_packet
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/7128/diffs?diff_id=413288788&start_sha=89555bc58123088bbaeb22a63825989dc23a1f5f)
changed title from **Draft: {-Qt: Implement total columns for traffic tables-}** to **Draft: {+tap: Adding flags for tap_packet_cb+}**

For anyone wanting to comment on this, I tried a variety of approaches for this. The main motivation is, to be able to show in the conversation and endpoint dialogs a percentage of the total values a display filter has. That is currently next to impossible, as the packets not touched by the dfilter are not used for the conversation tables. 

Before going this route I tried a variety of others, including running dual-taps or display filtering inside the dialogs. The second had the issue, that at the point of me looking at the packets, the tree object (required for filtering) is no longer available, and the first had especially issues for conversations, as in, the order of a conversation is determined by the first packet matched. That lead to situations where the tap for all packets had different ordered conversations than the filtered one. Now this could be fixed by a simple lookup, but doing this each time the user clicks somewhere (as required by the ModelView) lead to unbearable situations both on memory and cpu usage.

This approach now takes a different route. In dialogs where it is needed, I can tell the tap system and the data collection system not to filter at all, but rather store the data in a different space for total versus filtered. Granted, then the dialogs have to filter out rows where no matches have been found, but that can easily be done via a flag on the entry itself. I tried to avoid this approach initially, because of the vast impact on the tap system, but the underlying feature (n packets of x packets displayed) in the dialogs is a highly requested one and frankly, I can see the merit for packet analysis to have this number easily accessible.
